messages.subject: Call for testing
messages.body_plain:
Hi!

A new year, a new release. We certainly wanted to do this, a lot
earlier, but we are about to release a new version of RKWard, and we
need your help for testing. Many of you have probably been using
development snapshots later than version 0.7.0, already. For those who
have not, the most prominent new feature to look out for is the
live-previews that were added to the script editor window, including a
preview for R Markdown (.Rmd) scripts.

Beyond this, for this round of testing I am particularly interested in
the startup procedure on the various platforms (some more specific
instructions at the end of this mail). Ideally you will not even see a
difference in regular use, but internally I had to change a few things,
and I hope things work reliably across the different platforms and
configurations. In this area, reports of success are just as important
as reports of failure!

No release timeline has been set, yet. But depending on the outcome of
your testing, a release in January should be realistic.

Thanks!
Thomas

-- Mac users (and anybody with access to a Mac) --
- Get the latest DMG from
  https://binary-factory.kde.org/view/MacOS/job/RKWard_Nightly_macos/

- You will have to install R, separately (if you don't already have it).
  In theory, any version between 3.4 and 3.6 should work.

- No further configuration should be needed. RKWard should detect the
  newest version of R installed.

- I *believe* that all versions of MacOS from El Capitain (10.11)
  should work, however, the only version I could test was Mojave.

-- Windows users --
- Get the latest installer from
  https://binary-factory.kde.org/view/Windows%20MingW/job/RKWard_Nightly_mingw64/

- R 3.6.1 is included in the bundle. You should be able to start RKWard
  right away.

- If you have a separate version of R installed on this machine, please
  also try the following: Edit the rkward.ini file (inside the
  "bin" folder of your RKWard installation), changing the content to "R
  executable=auto". In theory this should detect your external R
  installation and use that.

-- Linux / BSD users --
- Compile the lastest git master version from source, or install one of
  the nightly builds, if we provide one for your distribution
  (https://rkward.kde.org/RKWard_Source_Repository.html).

- Should you have several versions of R installed, try
  switching between versions using the --r-executable commandline
  parameter.

messages.subject: RKWard 0.7.1 is released!
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

Before opening a bug report and to best address it either to RKWard or openSUSE, could someone confirm to be this behaviour outside of openSUSE's package (0.7.1)?

1. When the menu bar is set to be exported in the title bar (adding the "App Menu" button to the buttons of the title bar is enough nowadays).
2. Open RKWard directly, the app menu button is shown, and the menu is accessible.
3. Now open a script within RKWard, the app menu button disappears and the menu is not accessible anymore. Closing the script leave the app menu inaccessible, it doesn't come back.

I have reproduced this on two computers, both on openSUSE Tumbleweed and RKWard 0.7.1 installed from here:
https://build.opensuse.org/package/show/openSUSE:Factory/rkward

Of course, it doesn't happen when the appmenu is shown, as it is by default.

If it can be reproduced on another distribution, I'll open a true bug report against RKWard, otherwise, I'll contact the openSUSE's maintainers of RKWard.

Cheers,
Pierre.

messages.body_plain:
Hello all,

Thanks for the work! I really like the new R Markdown preview that I already tested via the 
daily snapshots recently. However, I am currently running into trouble installing the latest 
stable version for rkward (stable / devel / daily, does not matter). I am using Ubuntu 19.10, 
but the problem should also occur on the LTS version of Ubuntu. Here is what I tried:

- I added the "Inofficial Ubuntu Repository" via launch pad for "R shipped with Ubuntu by 
default" (https://launchpad.net/~rkward-devel/+archive/ubuntu/rkward-stable). 

- I used `sudo apt update` and `sudo apt install rkward` and get the following error: 

The following packages have unmet dependencies: 
rkward : Depends: r-base-core (>= 3.6.2-1eoan) but 3.6.1-4 is to be installed

Apparently, rkward 0.7.1 requires R >= 3.6.2. Unfortunately, this is not shipped with the 
Ubuntu repository for Ubuntu 19.10 (see here https://packages.ubuntu.com/search?
keywords=r-base&searchon=names&suite=eoan&section=all), also not for the LTS (see 
here https://packages.ubuntu.com/search?keywords=r-base&searchon=names&suite=bionic&section=all)

It is also not (easily) possible for me to update to R 3.6.2 because there is no CRAN-R 
release file for Ubuntu 19.10 (https://cran.r-project.org/bin/linux/ubuntu/).

If it is possible not to require R 3.6.2 for the newer rkward versions, that would be great. 
Any advice on how to solve the problem otherwise is also appreciated.

Best, 

Martin

messages.subject: RKWard 0.7.1 is released!
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

On Fri, 31 Jan 2020 10:46:37 +0100
Martin Papenberg <martin.papenberg at uni-duesseldorf.de> wrote:
> - I added the "Inofficial Ubuntu Repository" via launch pad for "R
> shipped with Ubuntu by
> default" (https://launchpad.net/~rkward-devel/+archive/ubuntu/rkward-stable). 
> 
> - I used `sudo apt update` and `sudo apt install rkward` and get the
> following error: 
> 
> The following packages have unmet dependencies: 
> rkward : Depends: r-base-core (>= 3.6.2-1eoan) but 3.6.1-4 is to be
> installed

please second-check your /etc/apt/sources.list. My guess is that you
have one of our PPAs marked "CRAN version of R" in your sources.list
(possibly in addition to the "plain" version; grep for "cran".

The dependency information is not hard-coded, anywhere, but generated,
automatically, at build-time, depending on the version of R on the
build-system. So, in this case, rkward has been built in a PPA that has
r-base-core 3.6.2-1eoan installed.

(RKWard itself is very modest in its requirements. When compiling from
source, you can go back all the way to R 3.0.0.)

Regards
Thomas
